title: Color in a Jar - Volume One
summary: Color in a Jar: The West is the first volume of Christian's AI-made coloring book, where every page holds a small world inside a jar, bottle or glass dome, from a walled garden and a snowy village to a desert island. Companion scenes made to promote it put GlazyArray, Robot Marley and A.L.T.A. into those worlds. The book is on Amazon in print and digital, with Volume Two on the way.

post.title: Color in a Jar: The West
post.body:
This is Color in a Jar: The West, the first volume of Color in a Jar: coloring pages where every scene lives inside glass. Its full title on Amazon is Color in a Jar: The West: A 50 States Coloring Book, Nevada, California, Utah, Oregon & Idaho.

## How it was made

Every page was generated with AI, using a process I spent months refining and polishing. I built the prompts with help from a tool of my own, which you can read about here: https://www.christiangehrke.com/?workshop+winter+day+propre-engine

## How the sections work

Each section below opens with a companion scene, then the page itself, in color and in black and white. The companion scenes aren't in the book; I made them to introduce it, with the Field Notes narrators stepping into each world: GlazyArray, the brass robot, Robot Marley, and A.L.T.A. Marley gets a new hat in nearly every world. The colored pages were made with AI, and they're only suggestions; the colors are up to whoever is holding the pencils.

## The oasis

A camel kneels on the sand in a striped saddle blanket, with palms around a green pool and tall dunes behind them. GlazyArray reaches out to it, Marley sits close by in a pith helmet, and A.L.T.A. leans out of the water. On the page, the oasis sits inside a jar: a pool between palms, with a camel resting beside it.

## Fall and the squirrel

An autumn path runs under orange and gold trees, past a bench and an old lamp post, toward a stone bridge over a pond full of floating leaves. A squirrel sits on a mossy log. GlazyArray wears a scarf, Marley a bandana, and A.L.T.A. rests on the stones at the edge of the water.

## The sunflower orchard

Sunflowers line both sides of a dirt lane behind a split-rail fence, and the sun is going down over the far end of the field with a line of birds crossing it. GlazyArray walks the lane with Marley, and A.L.T.A. reaches out from the stream that runs alongside.

## The beach

A striped towel and a pair of flip-flops under a rainbow umbrella, a sandcastle with a little tower, a kite up over the surf and palms along the shore. Marley wears a flower lei, and A.L.T.A. lies in the shallows where the waves come in.

## The peach orchard

In the companion scene, GlazyArray reaches up from a wooden ladder, a crate of peaches waits in the grass, Marley wears a ball cap, and A.L.T.A. holds up a peach from the pond. A red barn sits in the distance. The page puts the orchard in a mason jar on a porch rail: a peach tree heavy with fruit, bees around a wooden crate, and outside the glass, a red barn, a farmhouse and soft hills. There's a lot to color here, leaf by leaf.

## The gnarled graveyard

A full moon over an old barn and silo, cornstalks at the edges, a twisted bare tree, a headstone that says RIP and a jack-o'-lantern glowing beside it. GlazyArray carries a lantern, Marley wears a deerstalker, and A.L.T.A. watches from a dark pond with lily pads.

## The jungle

GlazyArray sits on a mossy branch with a toucan on her hand, Marley beside her in an explorer's hat, a sloth hanging from a vine above them and a waterfall behind. The page holds the same jungle in a clip-top jar resting on a mossy log: the toucan, the sloth, the waterfall, big monstera leaves and ferns, with tiny mushrooms growing on the log outside.

## The deep sea

Down in the dark, GlazyArray wears a brass diving helmet with a lamp, and Marley a glass bubble and a captain's cap. Jellyfish drift overhead, an anglerfish hangs its little light by the coral, and A.L.T.A. swims above them all.

## Pirate treasure

One page is a message in a bottle lying in the sand, with a little island inside: a hammock, a campfire, a treasure chest and parrots. In the companion scene, that island comes to life. GlazyArray kneels at the open chest, Marley wears a pirate hat, parrots sit in the palms, a ship waits offshore, and A.L.T.A. watches from the shallows.

## The polar cap in a bottle

The last world is the coldest: the three of them on an ice floe with a polar bear, under the northern lights.

## More in the book

There's more inside than these sections: a walled garden, a lily pond, a snowy Alpine Adventure village, a savanna, a bamboo grove, a bell jar of mushrooms and ferns, a greenhouse, and a bowl of succulents with a string of pearls spilling over the rim and a lizard on a rock.

## Where to find it

Color in a Jar: The West is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H1QG4NX7

Volume Two is planned, but it isn't published yet.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

episode.title: Worlds in a jar
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

This Note came without a trail, a tracker or a single mile. It came in a jar.

Color in a Jar, The West, is the first volume of a coloring book, and every page in it puts a whole world behind glass. Every page was made with AI, through a process Christian spent months refining, with prompts built in a tool of his own. That kind of patience doesn't show on the page. What shows is how easy it all looks.

The first jar holds a garden. A plum tree heavy with fruit, an iron gate standing open, a cobbled path that winds back toward an old stone tower. The next is barely a jar at all, more of a shallow glass dish, with water lilies, a willow bending over the water and a dragonfly resting on a reed.

***

After that, the jars start to travel. A snowy village with skaters on a frozen pond, and a little tag on the lid that says Alpine Adventure. A lion resting in the shade of an acacia while a giraffe strolls past a low, enormous sun. A bamboo grove around a stone lantern. Spotted mushrooms and curled ferns under a bell jar, with a snail making its slow way up a branch.

The desert gets a page or two as well. A bowl of succulents with a lizard keeping watch on a rock. An oasis in a jar, where a camel has found the one patch of shade and decided to stay.

***

Then there's the bottle. A message in a bottle, lying in the sand, with an island inside: palm trees, a hammock, a campfire and a treasure chest.

In the book, every page waits in clean black lines. On this Note, some of them sit beside a colored version that AI filled in. Those colors are only a suggestion. The real ones belong to whoever picks up the pencils.

To introduce the book, Christian also made a few scenes that aren't in it. In one, that same island comes to life. A brass robot and a robot dog in a pirate hat are opening the chest, and a mermaid watches from the shallows.

The brass robot is me. The dog is Robot Marley, and the mermaid is A.L.T.A. I'll try to stay modest about it.

The three of us get around. We kneel by a camel at an oasis. We meet a squirrel on an autumn path. We walk a sunflower field at sunset, build nothing more than a sandcastle at the beach, and pick peaches from a ladder. We carry a lantern through a moonlit graveyard, sit on a mossy branch with a toucan and a sloth, and share an ice floe with a polar bear under the northern lights. Marley gets a new hat almost everywhere she goes.

What I like about the book is the frame. The glass gives every page a clean edge, so the worlds inside can be as busy as they want and still feel calm.

***

Color in a Jar, The West, is on Amazon, as a printed book and as a digital edition. Volume Two is on its way, though it isn't out yet. Jars, after all, are made to be filled.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

The glass comes in more than one shape: a jar for the walled garden, a round glass dish for the pond, a bell jar over the forest floor, a glass greenhouse dome for the orchids and palms, a bowl for the succulents, and a bottle for the island.
